original_question: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponding to the boundary of P, determine a maximum hidden set of G, meaning a largest set of vertices no two of which are adjacent.
target_in_paper: Section 4.6, Open Problem 36 ("Maximum Hidden Set in Visibility Graphs")
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's exact target. It correctly identifies the input as the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P, includes the Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the boundary of P as part of the input, and asks for a largest set of pairwise nonadjacent vertices, which is exactly the paper's notion of a maximum hidden set.
missing_details: Make the input cycle explicit by naming it as a Hamiltonian cycle C of G that corresponds to the boundary of P.
State explicitly that G is the vertex visibility graph of P, so the vertices of G correspond to the vertices of the polygon.
Phrase the task as computing a maximum-cardinality subset H ⊆ V(G), not just 'determine' informally.
Use the paper's exact terminology 'hidden vertex set' or explicitly note the paper's equivalence: hidden vertex set = independent set.
refined_question: Given as input a graph G that is the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon P and a Hamiltonian cycle C of G corresponding to the boundary of P, compute a maximum hidden vertex set of G; that is, find a subset H ⊆ V(G) of maximum cardinality such that no two vertices of H are adjacent in G.
equivalent_formulation: Given as input the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle C of G corresponding to the boundary of P, compute a maximum independent set of G.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Open Problem 36 almost verbatim. In Section 4.6, the paper states: given the visibility graph of a simple polygon together with the Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the boundary, determine the maximum hidden set. The surrounding text in Section 4.6 explicitly defines a hidden vertex set as an independent set, so the independent-set formulation is an exact paper-approved reformulation. The nearby context in Section 4.4 defines the Hamiltonian-cycle input and shows that supplying this cycle is a meaningful added-information variant, while Section 1 provides the definition of the polygon visibility graph itself. The paper also motivates this exact narrowing by noting that the unrestricted maximum hidden vertex set problem is NP-hard, whereas the complexity may change when the boundary Hamiltonian cycle is supplied, and that a special convex-fan case is already solvable in O(ne) time.
